title: Dual-mode control plane upgrade: staged shadow + throttled promotion for VPC private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We need a low-risk, fully-automated upgrade flow for private (VPC) control plane upgrades that combines a shadow validation phase with a throttled promotion (traffic-throttled canary) and tenant-aware health scoring. The goal is zero-customer-downtime upgrades for most tenants and rapid, observable rollback when regressions are detected. This ticket implements the 'dual-mode' upgrade controller (upgrade-controller-v2) and accompanying Terraform/IaC changes.
description_2: Motivation: Current staged promotion approaches rely on coarse traffic slices and manual checks; incidents in Q4 showed slow detection of correctness regressions for control plane components (kube-operator, config reconciliation). For private customers we must minimize blast radius while enabling automated rollouts tied to telemetry. The dual-mode flow (shadow + throttled promotion) provides strong validation without affecting production latencies.
description_3:
Design proposal:
- Phase A (Shadow Validation): deploy new version alongside current control plane in tenant VPCs using traffic shadowing/mirroring. Requests are mirrored (no write effects) to the candidate control plane; responses are collected into a diff/validation pipeline. Run deterministic probes (api-smoke, reconcile-smoke) and non-deterministic sampling for longer-running paths.
- Phase B (Throttled Promotion): promote candidate to receive a small percentage of live traffic (0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with exponentially increasing windows. Promotion windows are controlled by the upgrade-controller-v2 state machine and Terraform flags.
- Health scoring: compute a tenant-aware health score combining 1) API success-rate, 2) median p95 latency, 3) reconciliation drift rate, 4) operator CPU/RAM and restart counts, and 5) rate of config-apply failures. Each metric has a weight and thresholds. A promotion gate requires health_score >= 0.98 over the evaluation window.
- Rollback and quarantine: automated rollback on sustained health_score degradation; optionally quarantine affected tenants for manual triage. Rollbacks are orchestrated with Terraform apply targets and operator-level drain hooks to avoid resource leaks.
- Terraform/IaC: new module private/controlplane/upgrade which exposes: image_tag, rollout_strategy (shadow+throttle), initial_traffic_pct, health_gate_config (metric_weights, thresholds), mirror_config, and dry_run flag. Module includes preflight 'drift and precheck' job that validates KMS access, tenant RBAC, and snapshot compatibility prior to promotion.
- Observability: add per-promotion dashboards and an aggregated promotions timeline. Events emitted to central event store with promotion_id for traceability. Add a canary_trace_id header to mirrored requests for correlation.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Shadowing vs. blue/green: shadowing avoids stateful data writes and tenant DB indirection but requires robust request mirroring and synthetic user traffic to exercise reconciliation code paths. Blue/green would be simpler for stateless APIs but is riskier for multi-tenant reconciliation.
- Traffic throttling granularity: we will implement per-tenant throttling where supported; otherwise use region/cluster slices. Per-tenant throttling reduces blast radius but increases orchestration complexity.
- Schema migration support: control plane will surface migration compatibility flags; the module must block promotion if non-backwards-compatible migration detected.

Acceptance criteria:
- upgrade-controller-v2 runs automated shadow validation in a canary tenant and produces a validation report (pass/fail) within 30 minutes.
- Throttled promotion increments automatically when the health_score meets configured thresholds and halts/pivots on failures.
- Terraform module exists and can be used by private deploys to start an end-to-end upgrade with a single apply (dry-run -> shadow -> throttled promotion).
- Dashboards and alerting for promotions + synthesized incident postmortem template are created.

Workplan (high level):
1) Implement health scoring prototype + synthetic probe suite (ENG-142400 ref).
2) Add request-mirroring infra and correlation header to runtime (PR link below).
3) Build upgrade-controller-v2 state machine and promotion orchestration.
4) Terraform module + preflight checks and gating.
5) Observability dashboards and alerting.
6) Run pilot in internal tenant pool, iterate thresholds, then run a staged rollout to 3 customer VPCs.

Progress updates (chronological):
- 2025-02-10 (Aisha Patel): Ticket created with initial design summary. Priority escalated after postmortem from incident RP-2024-11.
- 2025-02-12 (Marco Chen): Prototype health scoring algorithm implemented (local) and synthetic probes added. See branch health-score-proto.
- 2025-02-15 (Priya Singh): Terraform preflight checks spec added — includes kms access, snapshot-compat, and operator-version compatibility matrix.
- 2025-02-18 (Marco Chen): Shadow request mirroring implemented in runtime; merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/789. Added canary_trace_id header for correlation.
- 2025-02-20 (Khaled Omar): Observability events schema proposed; agreed on promotion_id and phase tags.
- 2025-02-21 (Design Review): UX for promotion dashboard reviewed by Priya and Marissa. Feedback: include a compact per-tenant health timeline and explicit 'quarantine' action in UI.
- 2025-02-24 (Marco Chen): upgrade-controller-v2 initial state machine merged to staging (https://github.com/redwood-inference/upgrade-controller/pull/214). It supports shadow -> pct promotion -> full promotion -> rollback.
- 2025-02-26 (Aisha Patel): Ran internal pilot against 5 staging tenants. Observed false positive on reconciliation drift metric for tenants with high background config churn. Adjusted drift metric smoothing and increased evaluation window to 10 minutes.
- 2025-02-28 (Marco Chen): Terraform module first pass completed; published module under upgrade-module branch. Preflight job integrated as a GitHub Actions workflow.

Open questions / blockers:
- KMS cross-account permissions for some enterprise tenants remain unresolved (security team ticket SEC-559). Promotion must block until resolved.
- Per-tenant throttling requires a runtime admission control hook; runtime team estimate 2 sprints. If delayed, rollout will use region-slices instead.
- Need legal sign-off for mirrored request retention (privacy policy alignment).

Next steps (short term):
- Resolve SEC-559 with Security & SRE (owner: Priya Singh). Target: 2025-03-07.
- Finish per-tenant throttle admission hook prototype (owner: Marco Chen). Target: 2025-03-14.
- Run first customer pilot with 3 low-risk customers and produce runbook + annotated postmortem template. Target: 2025-03-21.

Review notes (from reviewers):
- Priya Singh (2025-02-21): Approved design; requested explicit fallback to blue/green for tenants with strict compliance.
- Khaled Omar (2025-02-19): Observability & events schema feedback applied.
- Security (2025-02-22): Requested additional proof of KMS least-privilege; security_review_required flagged true.

Acceptance tests (manual/automated):
- Automated: run promote-e2e test that spins up fake tenant, performs shadow validation with synthetic traces, then runs throttled promotion and asserts health_score progression.
- Manual: runbook checklist for operators to start an emergency rollback; validate that rollback executes within the operator SLO (<= 5 minutes to traffic pivot).

Notes for QA/Oncall:
- When starting a promotion, include promotion_id in runbook and Slack alert. QA should validate reconciliation paths using golden-config fixtures.
- Oncall playbook: if more than 3 tenants show p95 latency > baseline+200ms for 10 minutes during promotion, immediately pause promotion and notify owners.

Sub-issues / follow-ups: ["ENG-142400", "ENG-142410", "ENG-142430"]

Last updated summary (2025-02-28): Core controller and module prototypes exist in staging. Shadowing, health scoring, and promotion orchestration are validated in internal tenants. Remaining blockers are KMS permissioning and per-tenant throttling hook. Next milestone: first external customer pilot (2025-03-21).
